Time carries us forward. Some experiences stay with us, returning to our thoughts long after the moment has passed. We might find ourselves dwelling on something without quite knowing why, ruminating, trying to understand a feeling that never quite settles into words. There is a distance between experiencing and knowing what it means to us. Time passes in between, but understanding doesn’t always follow. Some things remain unresolved, held somewhere between memory and feeling, familiar yet difficult to explain. Michael Samuels works with furniture and objects from decades past, carefully sourcing pieces for the qualities of their materials and surfaces. Marks, old paint and fingerprints left by use record the passage of time, the accumulation of lives lived with these objects. Through reconfiguration, their original functions fall away.
